payload.author: plengauer
payload.body:
The curl instrumentation has special handling for API calls to LLMs. However, if a 5xx error is returned because of an internal server-side error, and curl is configured to retry, a second span will be created, but nobody reads the forward pipe and some attribtues will be on the the wrong span. All these spans shall have the request attributes, but only the last succeeding one shall have the response attributes.

Right now the implementation parses stderr of curl to read metadata of the http request. the api part parses stdout to read the response and also gets provided the request via file. so the part parsing the stderr creates the spans (or retrieves the span id from somewhere else unrelated to this) and then forwards it to the part that parses the response. the response part needs it because it needs to know where to put its attributes. however, the api/response reading part only reads the pipe to transfer the span id only once. because it assumes an api call is made, it fails or not, but thats it. one request, one span. however, if the api responds with 500 or 429 curl may retry. and then a new span is created, a new span is forwarded by the part parsing stderr of curl, but the api part has already given up. it doesnt read the span fordward again. its actually blocked in trying to read a valid json from stdout of curl, so it doesnt even get a chance to read it.

the purpose of this issue is to fix that. the approach should be generalized. every span shall be forwarded as already done, but then as a second part the pipe shall be used to pass on the http status code, and as a third an END marker. so it shall send three lines at three different points in its lifecycle. this will then give the api/response part the chance to (1) when the first line (span handle) is received to put all the request attributes on it, (2) when the http response is received to decide on whether it then wants to wait for a response and start parsing stdout of curl at this point only, and then (3) the end will be read when its done, just to make the stderr part block from ending the span before all attributes are set.

we additionally have to solve the fact that if at any point curl terminates because of an internal error or because never a valid http response is received, there shall be a special marker that is always checked for and simply aborts the API reading part. lets call that "TERMINATE".

also make sure that if terminate is eventually reached and we are opting out, that we simply append a simple cat at the end to make sure we dont swallow any stdout accidentally

payload.author: Vlaaaaaaad
payload.body:
**TL;DR**: `otelcol-contrib: command not found` error on ARM runners

Hey,

It looks like there's a small ARM gap that breaks Thoth on `ubuntu-24.04-arm` runners. On those runners `arch` returns `aarch64` but the OpenTelemetry Collector release assets use `arm64` in their filenames (e.g. `otelcol-contrib_0.152.0_linux_arm64.deb`).

`actions/instrument/job/inject_and_init.sh` only normalises `x86_64 -> amd64`:

```bash
grep "$(arch | sed 's/x86_64/amd64/g')"
```

Because `aarch64` is not mapped to `arm64`, the `grep` finds no matching asset. The pipeline still creates an empty file at `/var/cache/apt/archives/otelcol-contrib.deb` via `tee`, which then causes:

```
dpkg-deb: error: unexpected end of file in archive magic version number
```

`otelcol-contrib` is never installed, and the instrumentation eventually fails with:

```
line 6: otelcol-contrib: command not found
```

This is an **evil bug** as the action runs successfully but no telemetry data is sent! It took me a while to figure it out!

### LLM-proposed fix

I temporarily moved my jobs to non-ARM runners but allegedly there's an easy fix: align the arch mapping in `inject_and_init.sh` with the mapping already used everywhere else in this repo (`INSTALL.sh`, `actions/instrument/shared/install.sh`, `.github/workflows/build.yml`, `.github/workflows/test_shell.yml`):

```bash
grep "$(arch | sed s/x86_64/amd64/g | sed s/aarch64/arm64/g | sed 's/le$/el/g')"
```

I did not open a PR with the fix as I did not have the bandwidth to properly investigate and test the fix.
payload.title: otelcol-contrib fails on ARM runners

payload.body:
https://github.blog/changelog/2026-03-12-actions-oidc-tokens-now-support-repository-custom-properties/

GitHub Actions OIDC tokens now support repository custom properties as claims (prefixed `repo_property_*`). These are organization- or enterprise-managed governance attributes on a repository — things like team ownership, environment classification, cost centre, project name — configured once at the org level and automatically applied to all matching repos.

The job-level instrumentation already auto-discovers and injects rich resource attributes (cloud provider, region, process info, etc.) without requiring users to set `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` manually. Repository custom properties are the GitHub-native equivalent of that kind of metadata, and surfacing them as resource attributes would let teams correlate their telemetry by team, project, environment, etc. in their observability backends for free.

The implementation does not need the OIDC token. The job-level instrumentation already uses the implicit GitHub token, which has `metadata: read` permission by default and can call `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/properties/values` to retrieve the custom property values for the repository. These could then be added as resource attributes on all telemetry generated by the instrumentation, e.g. under a `github.repo.property.*` namespace (or whatever fits the existing naming conventions in the codebase).

Consider whether this should be opt-in (via a parameter) or automatic, given that custom property values may sometimes contain sensitive classification data that users would not want in telemetry.
payload.title: Expose repository custom properties as resource attributes in job-level instrumentation

payload.body:
For security reasons, we have to use a fine grained token for renovate, compliation of agentic workflows, version bumps, otel deployment.

current state:
the codeowners forces the right approval requests, BUT
*) the repo owner cant approve themselves because the are done under his token
*) after rebases the right review requests are not rerequested

possible solutions and why they dont work:
*) agentic autoapprove workflow that identifies the right PRs doesnt work because the approval would come from github-actions app, and that app is not (and cannot be because apps simply cannot) be the codeowner
*) running an agentic workflow just to rerequest the right reviews is very expensive
*) changing all automations do be done as per the github-actions bot and then auto approving all PRs from that author doesnt work because anything done by the github-actions bot will not trigger workflows for "safety" reasons
*) the rebaseWhen property of renovate is set to behind and cannot be changed because then conflicts would never auto-resolve. this is technically not a blocker and could be changed, but it only trades slightly less review rerequests against manual conflict resolution
*) app users are not possible because creating installation tokens (via actions) auto expire at the end of a job run. we would need to create installation tokens that dont expire for at least a few days
*) a single app where the private secret is in the <user>.github.io repo to create installation tokens and put them into the repos would work, but they auto-expire after one hour. which is way too little. if we rotate the tokens once a day, they need at least 2-3 days expiry
*) giving the user of the token bypass permissions is actually hurting, because it doesnt just ignore approvals and bypasses, it also ignored CodeQL checks and tests. it completely bypasses all checks.
*) no codeowners would allow for github action approvals via an agentic workflow, BUT normal PRs wont get approvers automatically assigned. maybe the best solve?

payload.body:
See the comment on this PR: https://github.com/plengauer/Thoth/pull/2273
It talks about an artifact update error, being that /dev/stderr is not openable.

Why this happens: renvoate is run as a docker container with the job-level instrumentaiton (described in the readme) active. this means, we are injecting into the docker container (agent.instrumentaiton.docker.sh). usually, because we cannot rely that inside a docker cotnainer, all executables are installed, we dont fork a new sdk process (in otel_init function from api.sh) but re-use the one from outside via setting an env var. I assume, that the docker script (node script inside the container) is resetting the entire env. this way, the information we are sending into the processes will get lost, and the subprocess that will be instrumented again (agent.instrumentation.node.sh) will try to create its own sdk.

This means, whenever we instrument a child in the node/python/java code that gets automatically injected in the agent.instrumentation.node/agent.instrumentation.python/agent.instrumentation.java subdirectories, we explicitly have to make sure that the env that is being used contains all env vars that start with "OTEL_" from the current process. This will solve the issue.

Additionally, it is weird that the error talks about /dev/stderr not being able to be opened. This is weird, because there is a check at the top of api.sh that checks if /dev/stderr is writable. This is not causing the issue, but its a weird symptom. if you find a more reliable check then the "[ -w /dev/stderr ]", please replace.

payload.body:
Right now, once  a month the autoversion workflow runs, it checks all commits since the last version increment, determins whether (according to sem conv) major, minor, or patch needs to be incremented and then changes the version accordingly (VERSION file) and opens a PR. When the PR is merged, the publish steps gets triggered because the VERSION file was touched and releases a new version.

We wanna maintain the same functionality, but eagerly push out patch version in case of bugfixes. To do this the behavior should be changed in the following way:
*) right now, all tags / releases of all versions are always on mine, no matter if mjaor, minor, or patch was bumped. In the future, this should remain the case for major and minor, however, for all patch releases, a branch based on the last minor release should be created. all patch tags and releases of that minor version will be on that release branch.
*) select a good common pattern for naming the release branch.
*) the autoversion workflow should still run once a month, BUT should only ever adjust major or minor versions, never patch. For this, the parameter "increment_threshold" should be set to "minor". this will cause the action to still classify some commits as patch but then wont increment the veresion.
*) every time a commit is pushed to main, there should be new workflow being run that is called "backport". this backport workflow will search the pull request and the according issue. if the issue has the bug label, the diff needs to be backported. if the PR / issue cannot be found, AI should be used to determine based on the commit message if its a bugfix only or a dependency update that is only a patch version. If its the case, the diff should be applied to the release branch of that minor version Additionally, in the same commit, the patch version should be bumped, and then pushed to the release branch. if no release branch exists yet, it should be created on the fly
*) the publish workflow must also be triggered on the release branch
*) the refresh demo workflow should not be triggered by patch releases. to do that, it should only be triggered when the release tag is on main.

However it would help me greatly if I had confirmation of the expected outputs of this instrumentation. Is it supposed to plug itself with an external OTEL collector or does it generate files only ? If you wish to know more about my issue, more details below 👇 

I am using the [Manual deployment of Job-level instrumentation](https://github.com/plengauer/Thoth?tab=readme-ov-file#manual-deployment-of-workflow-level-and-job-level-instrumentations) with a simple workflow. My goal is to be able to plug this into grafana and collect logs, traces, metrics from Github actions and then expand from there.

```
name: Validate Renovate Config

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      smee-url-traces: 
        description: "Unique url of smee.io to forward traces to local grafana. Must be different than metrics and logs url"
        required: true
        type: string
      smee-url-metrics: 
        description: "Unique url of smee.io to forward metrics to local grafana. Must be different than tracs and logs url"
        required: true
        type: string
      smee-url-logs: 
        description: "Url of smee.io to forward logs to local grafana. Must be different than traces and metrics url"
        required: true
        type: string

jobs:
  validate-renovate-config-if-needed:
    name: Validate Renovate config (if needed)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Instrument job otel
        uses: plengauer/Thoth/actions/instrument/job@v5.23.0              
        env:
          OTEL_SERVICE_NAME: 'test-plengauer-gh-otel'
          OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT: "${{ inputs.smee-url-traces }}"
          OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_METRICS_ENDPOINT: "${{ inputs.smee-url-metrics }}"
          OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_LOGS_ENDPOINT: "${{ inputs.smee-url-logs }}"
          OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL: 'http/json'
          OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_PROTOCOL: 'http/json'
          OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_METRICS_PROTOCOL: 'http/json'
          OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_LOGS_PROTOCOL: 'http/json'
          OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TIMEOUT: 500
          OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_TIMEOUT: 500
          OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_METRICS_TIMEOUT: 500
          OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_LOGS_TIMEOUT: 500
          OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER: otlp 
          
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@08eba0b27e820071cde6df949e0beb9ba4906955 # v4

      - name: Check smee urls can accept payloads
        run: |
          curl -X POST ${{ inputs.smee-url-logs }} -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"log":"from ${{ github.action }}"}'
          curl -X POST ${{ inputs.smee-url-metrics }} -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"metric":"from ${{ github.action }}"}'

payload.body:
external processes are used because handles are managed by the SDK. a pipe needs creating, before that a random  file name, then it needs to removed afterwards. echo and cat are builtins. if the sdk manages the handles, almost never information needs to be communicated back, except for traceparents.

the handle must be unique in the sdk, but with subshells spawning different processes but reusing sdks, that may be an issue. to avoid that, we could use the REAL pid. $$ is not the real pid, but always the pid of the toplevel shell. we could use tricks like read -r /proc/self/stat to really find our own process id in non bash shells where $BASHPID is not an option
